title: Fluent Forms Review
description: A contact form, created and submitted in WordPress. See the saved entry and the limits of this free-edition check.
homepageSummary: For site owners who need contact forms and a clear place to manage submissions.
metaDescription: A transparently scoped Fluent Forms WordPress plugin profile from KreativWP.
highlights: Official documentation describes a drag-and-drop builder and ready-made form types
The documented workflow includes submission management and reporting
Payment forms and integrations are supported in the product ecosystem
bestFor: Sites that need forms beyond a basic contact address, while keeping the editor workflow approachable.
researchScope: Created a free contact-form template, embedded it on a published page, submitted synthetic fields, and verified dashboard retrieval. Documentation provides context for features outside that workflow.
caveats: Form plugins handle personal data. Validate consent, retention, spam prevention, notification delivery, and the exact plan’s capabilities before publishing forms.
thumbnailAlt: Fluent Forms screenshot from its WordPress.org listing

handsOnTest.environment: Isolated local macOS PHP server; SQLite Database Integration; Chromium; free editions. Email sending disabled by a lab-only filter. No production accounts or site data.

checks.title: Create and embed
checks.detail: Created a free contact template through the plugin UI and embedded its shortcode on a published page.

checks.title: Submit and retrieve
checks.detail: Submitted synthetic name, email, subject, and message fields. The public success message appeared; one database entry and its dashboard row were verified.

limitations: Email sending was disabled, so notification deliverability is not established.
Payments, Pro integrations, spam handling, high-volume behavior, and production MySQL compatibility were not tested.
